name: Captain "Guegler"
summary: The captain Larry would call when he wanted off a remote site — his contact for the helicopter with call sign Rosethorn 007. Larry identifies him in uniform at the Huey in VN-0020: a man in his late fifties who had been in the military a long time, and who was always said to be a great pilot. The surname is remembered phonetically; Larry has rendered it Guegler, Guetler, Gutler, and Getler. He may be associated with the period around August 1965, when Larry was mistakenly reported as killed in action.
larrysRecollection: When I wanted to get out of here, I would call Captain Guetler. (VN-0015 comment, 2026-08-15.) Right facing camera in uniform, looking at camera is Captain Gutler / Getler / Guegler. He was in his late 50s and was in the military a long time. My father always heard that the captain was a great pilot. (VN-0020 comments, relayed 2026-08-15.)
researchNotes: Now photographed (VN-0020) and functionally placed: the aviation officer who controlled Larry's helicopter access via Rosethorn 007. A captain in his late fifties implies prior-enlisted or WWII/Korea service — a mustang profile that narrows roster searches usefully. Spelling candidates: Guegler, Guetler, Gutler, Getler, Gugler, Geigler, Giegler, Kugler. Magnification (2026-08-15) settled an earlier tension: the tape once read as possibly beginning 'J' is the standard U.S. ARMY tape below aviator wings, so nothing in the photo contradicts the identification; his own name tape is hidden behind the jacket panel. Further identity notes: research/people/captain-guegler.md. Possible association with the erroneous killed-in-action report of August 1965 remains unconfirmed.
